lines: Telo Ride talks to two companies besides itself: YouTube for video, and Google, with your own key, for real-world tiles. Nobody else.
Every response carries a Content Security Policy that says so: scripts, frames, images and connections, each with its short list.
A tracker's script, or a call home to anyone else, is refused by the browser before it leaves the device.
And every behaviour spec now runs the app under that policy. A single refusal fails the spec, so a new third party cannot slip in.
The policy is static: the offline shell is checked by its bytes, so styles stay inline, and nothing else does.
Behind it, a sign-in leaves no email, code, token or query string in any span, metric or log.
Home, under its policy, from a phone to the full screen.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
